meta.title: Gocci — mount Google Drive wherever you want on macOS
meta.description: Mount Google Drive on an external disk, or anywhere else, without macFUSE — and without the shared files you once opened cluttering the top of your drive. A small macOS menu bar app.

hero.title: Put Google Drive where you want it.
hero.tagline: Mount it on an external disk. No kernel extension. No clutter from files other people shared with you.
hero.note: Free and open source. The first launch shows an "unidentified developer" warning

problem.title: Why this exists
problem.lead: The internal disk was full, so Google Drive had to live on an external one. No tool would do it.

items.title: Google's own app
items.body: You cannot choose where it mounts. It lands on the internal disk, which had 42 GB free.

items.title: Mountain Duck
items.body: Its docs say a custom mount location is not honoured on macOS — it is always ~/Library/CloudStorage.

items.title: CloudMounter
items.body: The location is yours to pick. But every file you ever opened through a share link is listed at the top of the drive, with no setting to hide them.

items.title: Mounts anywhere
items.body: An external disk, or any folder you like. It mounts at login, and waits for the disk if it is not plugged in yet.

items.title: No kernel extension
items.body: It runs on rclone's NFS mount. Nothing to install, nothing to approve, no reboot. Just the app.

items.title: No shared items
items.body: Files other people shared with you are not listed. What you see matches My Drive in the browser.

items.title: Finder shows what is local
items.body: A badge per file: cloud only, downloading, or fully here. Right-click to send one back to the cloud.

how.title: How it works
how.body: rclone serves NFS on localhost and macOS mounts it. Files come down when you open them and stay in a cache. How long they stay, and how large the cache may grow, are yours to set.
points: Writing works as usual — copy and delete from Finder
Google Docs appear as .webloc files and open in the browser
rclone ships inside the app, pinned to a version that was tested by hand

steps.title: Install
steps.body: Download the DMG and drag Gocci into Applications. The first launch is met with an "unidentified developer" warning — allow it from System Settings → Privacy & Security.

steps.title: Connect Drive
steps.body: Create a drive remote with rclone config, and make your own client ID while you are there (rclone's shared one stops working during 2026).

steps.title: Pick the place
steps.body: Choose the mount point in Gocci's settings. From then on it mounts there every time you log in.

footer.built: A macOS menu bar app, by the author of Konechi
